_doc: Headwaters source registry - Chennai episodic sources. Schema + design notes: docs/specs/headwaters.md (local). Validate: npm run data:check. Baseline/accept: scripts/check-upstream-editions.ts --accept <id>.

sources.notes: NWMP annual River Water Quality data. Serves Chennai (4 rivers/10 stations), Bengaluru (Vrishabhavathi/Arkavathy/Dakshina Pinakini), Madurai (Vaigai 10059/10060). HOST CHANGED 2026-07-26: this entry used to point at the CPCB NICNET host (cpcb DOT nic DOT in, 164.100.58.91), which has ports 80 and 443 filtered from a residential India IP - so the watch could never fire. cpcb.gov.in (49.50.115.127) serves the same content over a valid TLS chain, so insecureTLS was removed. This is why the entry never checked successfully and carried no lastSeen; the 2026-07-21 baseline logged it as a CPCB outage, which was the wrong diagnosis. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to an earlier version of this note: the failure is PER HOST, not NICNET-wide. nmcg.nic.in sits on the same range (164.100.60.206) and returns 200 today, and nmcg-ngt-mpr-listing watches it successfully. Do not infer '.nic.in is unwatchable'. Verified-dead hosts are listed in UNREACHABLE_HOSTS in check-upstream-editions.ts and rejected at validate time (P5-8). Watch target is /nwmp-data/, which lists one year page per edition (nwmp-data-2012 ... nwmp-data-2025 as of 2026-07-26). A NEW EDITION SHOWS UP AS A NEW nwmp-data-YYYY LINK - that is the signal. /nwmp-data-2/ is a stub last updated 20 Nov 2018 and /wqm/ has no directory listing, so neither works for link-set. linkPattern matches year pages plus wqm/YYYY/ document paths, and deliberately excludes the site-wide boilerplate PDFs (APPs_CPCB, gst_details, stqc-cert, E-GOVERNANCE, it_technical_activity) that appear on every CPCB page. Annual river data also resolves directly at https://cpcb.gov.in/wqm/{YEAR}/WQuality_River-Data-{YEAR}.pdf (2021-2024 verified, 5-15 MB each). CAUTION on the 2025 edition: the nwmp-data-2025 page exists and links WQuality_River-Data-2025.pdf, but that file is 465 KB / 2 pages of YAMUNA DATA ONLY (created 18 Jun 2026) and contains none of our rivers - grep for Cooum, Adyar, Vaigai, Vrishabhavathi, Mithi returns zero. The full national 2025 edition has not landed. ALWAYS confirm river coverage inside the PDF before treating a new year as actionable; the year page appearing is not sufficient.

lastSeen.edition: year pages through nwmp-data-2025 (2025 river file is Yamuna-only)

A Second Census has been announced nationally - this watch is how we would learn it landed. Lineage is Supabase, not a committed file.

sources.refreshMethod: manual (scripts/fetch-wris-groundwater.ts for the WRIS side; IN-GRES payload capture still open)
sources.notes: Dynamic Ground Water Resources assessment - block-level Safe/Semi-Critical/Critical/Over-Exploited classes and stage-of-extraction %, 16 Chennai-area blocks 2011-2024. IN-GRES is the canonical GW-assessment source for every city by user directive (see memory reference_ingres_groundwater); it is non-NICNET and reachable. CAVEAT: http-meta here watches the SPA build (Last-Modified 30 Jun 2026 + ETag, both verified 2026-07-26), NOT the assessment data itself - a redeploy will false-positive and a data-only update could be missed. Replace with an api-date watch once the IN-GRES payload capture lands. India-WRIS itself is a JS app with no watchable static endpoint, which is why it is not the url here.

sources.notes: Backs /chennai/lake-restoration project list and the Rs 4,450 Cr restoration fact in static-facts.ts. Serves no ETag or Last-Modified (verified 2026-07-26), so http-meta is out. linkPattern is scoped to the restoration project pages plus /download; a new river programme or a new document drop shows up as a new link. Known project pages 2026-07-26: cooum_restoration, adyar_river_restoration, adyar_river_restoration_ppp_mode, adayar_phase_one, adayar_phase_two, buckingham_canal_restoration, ennore_creek_eco_restoration. Both 'adyar' and 'adayar' spellings are live on the site, hence both in the pattern.

sources.publisher: TN Municipal Administration and Water Supply Department
sources.refreshMethod: manual - the commitments register names this as its primary re-check document
sources.notes: The MAWS Policy Note is the single richest annual statement of what TN says it is doing on urban water, and commitments-chennai.json names it in update_model as the April re-check document. KNOWN LIMIT: this watch catches a REVISION of the current note only. The filename is year-templated (maws_e_pn_{YYYY}_{YY}.pdf) and there is no TN policy-note listing page - /en/policy-notes, /policy-notes and tn.gov.in/documents/policy_notes all 404 (verified 2026-07-26) - so next April's edition needs the url-template detection method (P5-9 in the coverage audit). Until then, bump this url by hand each April. The WRD note (wrd_e_pn_{YYYY}_{YY}.pdf) sits on the same path pattern and is the Madurai analogue. MIGRATED to url-template 2026-07-26 (P5-9 shipped): the entry now probes maws_e_pn_{YYYY}_{YY}.pdf forward each run, so NEXT April's note is detected on publication instead of needing a hand bump. This supersedes the http-meta limitation described above.

CMWSSB's own system pages back the allocation ledger (1976 and 1983 Krishna instruments, Veeranam, the desal contracts), several supply-overview figures, and the 745 MLD / 200 MLD desal / 13,222 Mcft static facts. Upload filenames are date-stamped (e.g. 14Jul2026102630_TNUFIP-T1-UpdatedIEEReport...pdf), so a new board document appears as a new link - a strong, low-noise signal. Verified 2026-07-26: page 200, no ETag/Last-Modified, 12+ upload PDFs matched. The sibling page /sewerage-system carries the 745 MLD installed-treatment figure and should get its own entry if the two diverge. NOTE the host: cmwssb.tn.gov.in is live; chennaimetrowater.tn.gov.in is NOT reachable and was swept out of the citations on 2026-07-26.

sources.publisher: CEEW + Tamil Nadu Climate Change Mission
sources.ciBlocked: ceew.in returns 403 to ALL automation, not just CI runners - verified 2026-07-26 from a residential India IP with a full browser UA, on /publications, the publication page and /sites/default/files. Same class as ADB (likely TLS fingerprinting). The flag is used here to stop weekly false alarms; unlike the other ciBlocked entries a LOCAL run cannot check it either, so a standing CHECK-FAILED on local runs is expected and correct - it is a true statement that we cannot watch this source by fetch. Re-check from a real browser.
sources.refreshMethod: manual (browser download; the WEAP figures are hardcoded in weap-balance-tile.tsx)
sources.notes: Feb 2026 report behind the whole /chennai/climate-risk surface (6 sub-basins x 4 subthemes, 33 indicators) and the dashboard WEAP water-balance tile (unmet demand 2020 and 2050, business-as-usual). This is the ONLY source for those numbers and one of the few where the figures are hardcoded in a component rather than a data file - see dependsOn. 403 to automation, so treat CI check-failures as expected and re-check from a browser; ciBlocked keeps it from filing weekly false alarms.

The 9 resources on this dataset map 1:1 onto our flood layers: Chennai Inundation Points with Depth, Flooding Points in 2015, Flows 5/10/25/50/100/200 Year Return Period, Flood Hazard Zones Map. Underlying model is NCCR's C-FLOWS. Verified 2026-07-26: metadata_modified 2025-11-27T12:37:59. The 2020 hotspots layer comes from a SEPARATE dataset (chennai-floods-2020-data) which is not watched by this entry - register it separately if that layer starts carrying load-bearing numbers.

GCC's 2023 storm-water-drain survey: 115 resources (a master 2023 map plus one per ward) behind the 10,308-segment chennai-drainage.geojson, including the Good/Bad condition field that drives the ward drainage profile. Verified 2026-07-26: metadata_modified 2025-11-27T12:36:35. Pair source is chennai-basin-drainage-maps (5 resources: Basin Rivers and Streams, Buckingham Canal, Krishna Water Canal, Macro Drains, Micro Drains) - register separately if the basin layers start carrying numbers.
